clue.text: Armed throngs disconcerted the older women

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crowd of armed people has unsettled some elderly ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of ARMED THRONGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmothers are typically women of an older generation, the mothers of parents.

clue.text: Very ancient Greek makes observations 'on Turkish leader

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so it goes before

parts.note: eyes stand for looks or observations, as in 'all eyes'

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Greek man watches a Turkish chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts EYES above T, the first letter of 'Turkish' picked out by 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey hair goes with age, so the greyest is the oldest of all.

clue.text: A bar in a new development to do with the Middle East

definitions.text: to do with the Middle East

indicators.note: a new development turns the letters into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new bar opening in a building scheme in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new development' tells you to shuffle the letters of A BAR IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabian describes Arabia, the peninsula at the heart of the Middle East.

clue.text: Application for a coach

explanation.surface: A request for a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is steady hard work, and also an old French public stagecoach.

clue.text: A beast — all right, a mixed-up type

parts.note: OK means all right
pi (or pie) is printers' jargon for jumbled type

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a confused person as a fine but odd creature.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a printing term: metal type that has been spilt and mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: The top man determined to 'get a hearing device

parts.note: the head is the man at the top of an organisation
set can mean determined or resolved, as in 'set on going'

explanation.surface: The boss is resolved to obtain a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, worn over the ears for listening.

clue.text: About to join a girl — the one' with the big cigar!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is about to go out with a girl, the one with the big cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'girl' comes at the end of the answer; 'with' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regalia was a large, high-quality Havana cigar.

clue.text: Lessen stress somehow when there's turmoil

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Advice to reduce anxiety in troubled times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' tells you to rearrange the letters of LESSEN STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Restlessness is a state of agitation or unrest, much like turmoil.

clue.text: The looker round

parts.note: read not as someone glancing about but as the round thing that does the looking

explanation.surface: A person who gazes about them.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of sight is a ball, a round thing you look with.

clue.text: Periodical strike backed by a union

indicators.note: by here sets the single letter beside the reversed run, ahead of it
backed means the pair of words is written in reverse order

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical
lam means to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: A periodical industrial strike is supported by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns MAGLAM into MALGAM, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or combination, a union of different things.

clue.text: She took theatre-goers by storm!

parts.note: an actress who was a hit, whose surname is a word for a storm

explanation.surface: An actress was a sensation with audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Tempest was a celebrated English stage actress of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress's surname means a violent storm, and she won over audiences.

clue.text: Prolific character of ancient China

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T, a character
the Ming were a dynasty of old China

explanation.surface: A productive figure from Chinese history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter here, written as its spoken name.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or abundant, as a fertile, prolific place is.

clue.text: Detached in the main

explanation.surface: Someone aloof in most respects.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means aloof and narrow-minded, and literally of an island, set in the sea (the main).

clue.text: Nibbled at to occupy a short evening

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside the shortened word

parts.note: e'en is a contracted, poetic form of evening

explanation.surface: Someone snacked to fill a brief evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nibbled has been eaten in small bites.

clue.text: Terrifying affair of the dark horse

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A frightening episode involving a black horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream or ordeal.

clue.text: Drink makes us wind about in, say, turning right

indicators.note: about means the wind word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: turning says the abbreviation for 'say' is written backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A drink makes us gassy, turning things round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes GE from EG; 'about' puts IN, GE and R inside GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: A number recognized — about 22

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps around the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: seen means noticed or recognized
the answer to 22 down, an occasion

explanation.surface: Someone has noticed a figure of around twenty-two.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a whole number between sixteen and eighteen.

clue.text: Old painter entering 22 by mistake

indicators.note: entering means going inside the rearranged word
by mistake means the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, an occasion
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist wanders into an occasion by error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' turns EVENT into VETEN; 'entering' puts RA inside it before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone old and long-experienced.

clue.text: Salt — within moderation it rates as an essential

indicators.note: within means the letters are found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Salt in moderation counts as essential to diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' points to letters running from the end of 'moderation' through 'it' into 'rates'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Little work is available in the South-east — that's material

indicators.note: in means the unit goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
an erg is a tiny unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: There is not much employment in the South-East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric.

clue.text: Blast! The Italians don't like it!

definitions.text: Blast! The Italians don't like it!

parts.words: Blast! The Italians don't like it!
parts.note: read not as an oath but as a gust of wind that Italians dislike

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Italians disapprove of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The sirocco is a hot, dusty wind blowing from Africa over southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot oppressive wind is a blast unwelcome in Italy.

clue.text: Take someone else's place for comfort

explanation.surface: Stand in for someone to make them feel better.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to take over a duty from someone, and also to ease or soothe.

clue.text: Give the right call

explanation.surface: Make the correct decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to grant a claim, and also to name or style something.

clue.text: An occasion requiring uniform over a casual shirt

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: even means uniform or level
a T is a T-shirt, casual wear

explanation.surface: An event demands a uniform worn over a T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or occasion.

clue.text: This keeps the listener warm

parts.note: the listener is the organ of hearing, kept warm by a flap of a hat

explanation.surface: Something keeps an audience member cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap of a cap that covers and warms the organ of hearing.

clue.text: The fellow's style is certain to hold him back

indicators.note: to hold means the first word wraps around the other

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: back means that word is written backwards

parts.note: him refers to the fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A man's manner is bound to restrain him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MAN into NAM, which 'to hold' places inside SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname is a family name, how a person is styled.

clue.text: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!

definitions.text: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!

parts.words: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!
parts.note: read not as political wire-pullers but as troops who drew bowstrings

explanation.surface: Veterans who are experts at using influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen were soldiers who pulled back bowstrings to shoot.

clue.text: In confidence, there's no rude drunk allowed here

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: Discreetly, no rudeness is permitted in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' tells you to rearrange THERES NO RUDE; 'allowed here' is linking. The rose was an old symbol of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa, the Latin idiom, means secretly, privately.
